Vide instant revision petition, revisionist takes exception to the order dated 21.11.2022 (and consequent framing of formal charges dated 21.11.2022) passed by Ld. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, South- Crl Rev No. 142/2023 Tek Chand. vs. State of NCT of Delhi Page No. 1 of 8 East District, whereby charges were directed to be framed against him (alongwith other accused) for offences u/s 120B and 420/471 IPC read with Section 120B IPC, in case FIR No. 216/03, Police Station Lodhi Colony titled as 'State Vs Tek Chand'.
2. Brief facts, as per prosecution version, may be taken note of:
It is the case of prosecution that co-accused namely Subhash, Karan, Yashpal, Uday Singh, Ram Kishan, Virender Singh and Subhash Chand entered into a criminal conspiracy with revisionists/accused (working as a Clerk/Dealing Assistant in the concerned SDM Office) & with other co- accused, in and prior to July 2002, to get job of Constable (GD) in BSF by procuring and using fake domicile certificate purportedly issued by SDM, Saraswati Vihar, Kanjhawla, Delhi.

8. The law regarding sufficiency of material which may justify the framing of charges against accused and also the court's decision to proceed against him in a given case is well settled.
The court has to eschew itself from embarking upon a roving inquiry into the last details of the case.
It is also not advisable to adjudge whether the case shall ultimately end in conviction or not.

If the criminal court, on consideration of the Crl Rev No. 142/2023 Tek Chand. vs. State of NCT of Delhi Page No. 3 of 8 material submitted with the charge-sheet finds that a grave suspicion exists about the involvement of the accused in the crime alleged, it is excepted to frame the charge and put the accused on trial.

12. At the outset, I may mention here that another revision petition No. 17/2023 (preferred by co-accused Subhash and Karan Singh) was disposed off by me (as ASJ-05, South-East) vide judgment dated 19.04.2023 inter alia with following observations:-
"In the instant case, copy of the domicile certificates annexed with the application form submitted on behalf of revisionists before concerned BSF Authorities show that they are residents of A4/189, Sultanpuri, Delhi-41.

However, the statement of Sh.
Rajesh Kumar, the concerned owner of said premises was recorded by IO who stated that the revisionists did not reside at the given address at any point of time.
Therefore, in view of the statement of said witness, it is clear that both the revisionists were not residents of Delhi as shown in the said domicile certificates.
13. As per the written reply dated 09.05.2003 furnished by Sh. Kartar Singh, the concerned SDM, the domicile certificate of revisionist Subhash S/o Sh. Shree Ram was not issued by him.
Therefore, it is clear that the copy of the domicile certificate annexed with the application form of the said revisionist is a forged document.

Though Ld. Counsel vehemently argued that in view of the FSL report, it has been proved on record that the application form is not in handwriting of said revisionist,
however in my considered view, the very fact that revisionist Subhash was the beneficiary of the said application which inter alia bears his photograph also, a grave suspicion arises that it was revisionist Subhash only at whose instance, the forged document was used.

14. Though the author of the said forged domicile Crl Rev No. 142/2023 Tek Chand.
vs. State of NCT of Delhi Page No. 5 of 8 certificate could not be ascertained, however it is clear that the said revisionist alongwith other co-accused (since not apprehended) entered into a criminal conspiracy to obtain a forged domicile Tek Chand vs State on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33894375/
3 certificate and in pursuance of said criminal conspiracy, obtained the same and used the same as genuine by annexing its copy.

sentences.text:
Therefore, grave suspicion for charging revisionist for offence u/s 120B IPC and 471 IPC read with section 120B IPC arises against revisionist Subhash.
15.
As far as revisionist Karan is concerned, admittedly the domicile certificate was issued by Sh. Kartar Singh, the concerned SDM.
Therefore, the said certificate would not fall within definition of false document as defined under section 464 IPC so as to term the same as forged document.

However, in view of statement of Sh. Rajesh Kumar, the concerned owner of the premises i.e. A4/189, Sultanpuri, Delhi-41, it is clear that the said revisionist did not reside at the said premises at any point of time.

Though the record of the concerned file at the concerned SDM office could not be traced, however it can be safely assumed that the revisionist must have represented himself as a resident of A4/189, Sultanpuri, Delhi-41 for applying for the requisite domicile certificate and the concerned issuing authority was induced to issue the said certificate to the said revisionist due to the said deception i.e. showing himself as resident of Sultanpuri, Delhi.

Therefore, a grave suspicion arises that the said revisionist alongwith co-accused Tek Chand and other co- accused i.e. tout Gupta (since not arrested) entered into a criminal conspiracy to deceive the concerned issuing authority in issuing him a domicile certificate and in pursuance of said criminal conspiracy, induced the said authority to issue him such certificate despite not being resident of Delhi.
Therefore, grave suspicion arises against the revisionist for offence u/s 120B IPC and 420 IPC read with section 120B IPC.

sentences.text: Further, it is evident from record that concerned BSF Authorities were induced to proceed with processing of applications of revisionists Karan and Subhash as they had annexed the said domicile certificate showing themselves to be the resident of Delhi which was one of the essential requirement for participating in the said recruitment process.

In my considered view, for want of requisite domicile certificate,
the applications of revisionists would have been rejected by the concerned BSF authorities at the outset without processing the same further.
Therefore, a case u/s 417 IPC read with section 120B IPC is also made out against both the revisionists.

17. To summarize, on the basis of material available on record, a grave suspicion arises against revisionist Subhash so as to charge him for offences u/s 120B IPC, 471 IPC read with section 120B IPC and u/s 417 read with section 120B IPC.

Further,
grave suspicion arises against revisionist Karan Singh so as to charge him for offence u/s 120B IPC, 420 IPC read with section 120B IPC and u/s 417 read with section 120B IPC.
13.

There is nothing on record to suggest that my aforesaid findings (rendered in Crl.
Revision Petition No. 17/2023) has been altered / modified / set aside by any of the Tek Chand vs State on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33894375/
4 Superior Courts.
Therefore, same have attained finality.

14. Therefore, in view of my said findings ( rendered in Crl. Revision Petition No.
17/2023) and other material available on record, it is held that a grave suspicion arises against revisionist so as to charge him for offence punishable u/s 120B,
420/471 r/w 120B IPC.
